subject.title: fix(browser): use public ssrf runtime import in CDP proxy bypass

question: Should `registerManagedProxyBrowserCdpBypass` remain private to bundled browser/runtime code, or be promoted to the public `openclaw/plugin-sdk/ssrf-runtime` contract?
rationale: The current PR assumes a public SDK export that does not exist, while current source and guardrails keep managed proxy bypass helpers on a private owner-scoped surface.

options.title: Keep Owner-Scoped Private Access
options.body: Repair packaged browser resolution through the existing private bundled-plugin mechanism or another narrow private seam without exposing the bypass helper publicly.

options.title: Promote To Public SDK
options.body: Add the helper to the public SSRF runtime subpath only with explicit docs, export metadata, guardrails, and compatibility/security proof.

options.title: Choose A Sibling Canonical Fix
options.body: Pause or close this import-only branch if maintainers pick an open sibling PR or new replacement branch for the same regression.

recommendation.title: Keep Owner-Scoped Private Access
recommendation.body: Repair packaged browser resolution through the existing private bundled-plugin mechanism or another narrow private seam without exposing the bypass helper publicly.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice is the SDK/package public-private boundary, and `steipete` authored adjacent private SDK declaration hardening.
